call_points.text: AUM growth guidance maintained at 21-23% despite current 25% run rate due to potential BT-out pressure.
Sambhav segment to reach ₹600 Cr monthly disbursement run rate by end of FY27.
Potential 6-7% PBT impact from proposed insurance commission caps, with only partial offset possible.
Indian home loan industry is projected to grow at 14-16% CAGR through FY28 to reach ₹60-63 lakh Cr.
Management aims to reduce Opex to NTI ratio to 14-15% over the medium term via process digitalisation.
Targeting 5% market share in incremental home loan originations from ~2.5-2.7% currently.
Medium-term GNPA target set at 40-60 bps as various credit portfolios mature.
Medium-term return guidance maintained at 2.0-2.2% RoA and 13-15% RoE.
Sambhav affordable home loans targeted to reach ~20% of home loan acquisitions in the medium term.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated focus on Sambhav affordable segment

call_points.text: FY26 NIM moderation of 7 bps outperformed the initial guidance band of 15-20 bps.

operating_notes.text: Disbursements in FY26 rose 27% YoY to ₹64,616 Cr, with Q4 disbursements at ₹17,506 Cr (+23% YoY).
Lease rental discounting AUM grew 44% YoY to ₹31,531 Cr as of March 31, 2026.
In Q4FY26, changed presentation of recoveries against written-off loans from Other Operating Income to Loan Losses and Provisions across all periods.
Average ticket size for home loans at origination stood at ₹48.4 lakh, with average customer salary of ₹15.0 lakh.
Sambhav Housing (near-prime and affordable) disbursement run rate was ~₹410-425 Cr per month.
FY26 borrowing mix stood at 43.9% NCDs, 40.8% bank loans, 10.0% NHB, and 5.3% CP.
Portfolio mix as of March 2026 stood at 54.1% Home Loans, 22.4% LRD, 11.5% Developer Financing, and 10.8% LAP.
Allotted secured redeemable NCDs at face value of ₹1,00,000 each aggregating to ₹2,000.6723 Cr at 8.25% p.a. maturing on 27 May 2031.
Allotted 2,00,000 secured redeemable NCDs at face value of ₹1,00,000 each aggregating to ₹1,991.8320 Cr at 7.83% p.a. maturing on 18 May 2029.
Borrowing mix: money market 52%, bank borrowings 38%, NHB refinance 10%; relationships with 18 banks.
Sambhav Housing: ~65% of customers have bureau score above 750; salaried mix 68%; average ticket size ₹28 lakh, affordable ticket size ~₹18 lakh, affordable one-third of Sambhav disbursements.
Assignments have historically run at 12-13% of AUM; portfolio yield 8.9% and gross spread 1.7% in Q1FY27.
Q2FY27 product AUM: home loans ₹85,224 Cr, LRD ₹37,988 Cr, developer finance ₹16,904 Cr, LAP ₹16,382 Cr, others ₹1,707 Cr.
H1FY27 assigned loans of ₹4,056.46 Cr across 2,713 accounts and acquired loans of ₹2,660.36 Cr across 14,428 accounts.
Impairment Reserve of ₹25.09 Cr created as Ind AS 109 allowance was below IRACP norms.
Sambhav housing constitutes 16% of overall home loan originations in Q2FY27.
Cost of funds reduced to 7% in Q2FY27 from 7.2% in Q1FY27.
Internal floating rate (PLR) increased by 15 bps effective 16 October 2026.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹2,902.61 Cr, net profit ₹669.19 Cr (+14.1% YoY).
Bajaj Housing Finance released its Q4FY26 presentation: AUM rose 23% YoY to ₹1,40,706 Cr, PAT grew 18% in FY26 to ₹2,560 Cr with GNPA at 0.27%.
Bajaj Housing Finance Limited held a conference call on 27 April 2026 at 6:00 PM IST for Q1 FY2026 results, with recording available at the company’s website.
Niraj Bajaj, on behalf of Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd.’s Promoter Group, disclosed no new encumbrances on shares held as of April 3, 2026, per SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
Bajaj Housing Finance released an updated investor presentation outlining medium-term targets including 5% incremental HL market share and 14-15% Opex/NTI.
Bajaj Housing Finance allotted 95,500 secured redeemable NCDs aggregating to ₹955.00 crore on private placement.
Bajaj Housing Finance allotted ₹1,991.83 crore of secured redeemable NCDs on private placement.
Q1FY27 call (29 Jul 2026): PAT up 23% to ₹715 Cr on 24% AUM growth, but management guided FY27 NIM 20-25 bps lower and credit cost back to 10-15 bps.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹3,250.57 Cr, net profit ₹756.97 Cr (+17.7% YoY).
Bajaj Housing Finance reported Q2FY27 PAT of ₹757 Cr, up 18% YoY on AUM growth of 25% to ₹1,58,205 Cr.
Bajaj Housing Finance Limited hosted the Q3FY27 conference call on 16 October 2026 at 17:30 IST, sharing audio recording and presentation via its website.
Chief Financial Officer Gaurav Kalani resigned effective January 22, 2027, after over 23 years with the Bajaj group.
Bajaj Housing Finance reported Q2FY27 PAT of ₹757 Cr (+18% YoY) as AUM crossed ₹1.5 lakh Cr and Sambhav disbursements hit ₹500 Cr/month.

watchlist.response: Spread is flat at 1.7%; portfolio yield fell as higher-yield legacy loans attrite and lower-yield new loans come in, with some further compression expected through the year
watchlist.text: Why NIM fell 13-14 bps when yields were flat and cost of funds fell 7 bps

watchlist.response: Yes: a ~₹2,300 Cr assignment released Stage 1 provisions, and no repeat of last year's Stage 2 coverage top-up; full-year guide stays 10-15 bps
watchlist.text: Credit cost of 5 bps versus 10-15 bps full-year guide — any one-offs

watchlist.response: LAP provisioning is DPD-formula based with pool plus/minus; the developer finance account was already provided at 48-49% in Stage 2 versus 33-34% required at 90 DPD
watchlist.text: Stage 2 to Stage 3 migration in LAP and developer finance without a provisioning increase

watchlist.response: Largely sideways: continued investment plus NIM compression offsets efficiency gains
